text:
maria: Heads up — found a dev backup archive in s3-dev with no SSE metadata. Looks like backup-agent v1.2.0 uploaded it during the last deploy. Unsure if PROD was touched. @sec-oncall @jon

jon: Yikes. Which object?

maria: s3://redwood-dev-backups/2026-03-18/db-dump-20260318.tar.gz

sec-oncall: :rotating_light: Is it plaintext? Size? Any SSE headers?

maria: Size ~1.2G, head-object shows no server-side-encryption header.

maria: ```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-dev-backups --key db-dump-20260318.tar.gz
{
  "ContentLength": 1283456789,
  "ContentType": "application/x-tar",
  "ETag": ""..."",
  "Metadata": {}
}
```

devops: Which principal uploaded it? CloudTrail?

maria: CloudTrail shows PutObject by arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-agent-role (backup-agent service account) at 2026-03-18T02:14:10Z

sam: That service version had a toggle for SSE enforcement, IIRC. Did the config flip to off?

ashley: Immediate triage checklist: 1) Revoke/rotate the SA write credentials. 2) Quarantine the object (copy to secure bucket). 3) Either re-encrypt and re-ingest or delete if it's disposable. 4) Start incident log/postmortem.

jon: I'll revoke the role session tokens now. @maria can you snapshot MD5/checksum + CloudTrail link for audit before any deletions?

maria: Yep. MD5: abc123def456... Uploaded checksum and CT link to the incident ticket: https://tracker.internal/t/INC-2026-314

sec-oncall: Also need to verify KMS grants and key policy: run `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-backup` and `aws kms get-key-policy`. Make sure there isn't an unintended grant to backup-agent-role that bypasses conditions.

sam: I ran `list-grants` earlier — there is a grant to role/backup-agent-role with Encrypt/Decrypt, but it has GrantConstraints with `encryptionContext: environment=prod`. So the grant shouldn't authorize prod-contextless encrypts in dev.

maria: Looks like the agent did a plain S3 PUT without SSE-KMS. Role IAM allowed S3:PutObject against the dev backup bucket without a condition requiring x-amz-server-side-encryption. So not a KMS grant bypass — an IAM condition omission.

ashley: Root cause hypothesis: policy gap permitting unencrypted puts into backup buckets for non-prod namespace. Fix: add IAM explicit Deny if `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` not present or not equal to `aws:kms`. Apply to all backup buckets.

jon: I'll open a policy change PR against infra-iam to add that Deny condition and require SSE-KMS for backup prefixes. Will also enforce bucket policy requiring SSE.

devops: Add an audit rule: CloudWatch Event / EventBridge rule to detect PutObject where `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` header missing -> alert #eng-security and auto-create ticket.

sam: For remediation I'm copying the object to quarantine: `s3://redwood-sec-quarantine/2026-03-18/db-dump-20260318.tar.gz` and will re-encrypt using CMK `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd-ef01`. We'll keep a manifest with original CT entry.

sec-oncall: Do we need legal/customer escalation? It's a dev bucket — no customer PII expected. But run a quick grep for email/SSN patterns in the dump to be safe before marking low severity.

maria: Ran a quick grep sample across the dump archive headers and a subset of rows; no email pattern matches and no clear PII. Marking incident severity: low. Postmortem owner: @ashley.

jon: Action items summary: 1) Policy PR to require SSE-KMS on backup buckets. 2) Backup-agent config bump to fail when SSE not set and release patch. 3) Revoke/rotate role tokens. 4) Quarantine & re-encrypt or delete. 5) EventBridge alert for unencrypted put. 6) Postmortem + docs.

maria: Initial actions done (revoked sessions, copied file to quarantine, saved audit artifacts). I'll follow up with the postmortem draft tomorrow morning.

sec-oncall: Nice work team. Let's also add an integration test for the backup pipeline that asserts S3 objects have SSE headers to prevent regressions. :white_check_mark:
